name: Light Rose
lede: Light Rose is a pale pink, a much lighter and softer step off [[rose]], the flower-named color that for most of history simply meant red.

sections.title: A modifier on an old flower name
sections.body:
The name is built by grammar: "light" over the parent [[rose]], which did not settle into today's pink until new dyes and new garden roses gave it a color of its own [1]. Three sources converge on this exact pale step: Ridgway's 1912 atlas at plate I, hue 3, tone f; the ISCC-NBS lists of 1955; and the Maerz and Paul dictionary, which gives 1905 as its first record, plate 1 G 7 [1]. Measured, it is far lighter and far less saturated than rose itself (lightness 85 against 55, chroma 22 against 85), closer to a baby pink [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[baby-pink|Baby Pink]], 3.1 units away, almost the same, with [[light-pink|Light Pink]] close behind at 4.1, more vivid [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this pale pink in only 1 of 23,781 paintings (as photographed), rarer than 86 percent of the named colors we track [2]. That single match, by Isaac Grünewald in 1917, plays as the painting's lightest color [2].

origin.first_recorded: 1905 (Maerz and Paul, plate 1 G 7); also Ridgway 1912, plate I; ISCC-NBS 1955
origin.source: Maerz and Paul, A Dictionary of Color

True or false: for most of its history, "rose" as a color word meant pink.

openers: For most of history "rose" meant red, not pink; this pale step only works because rose later came to mean pink too.
